answer: Picture each agent holding a lantern whose fuel is bonded stake; to sit at the network's vertex of trust it must burn real capital that peers can slash. A sybil operator splits one pot of nectar across many dim lanterns, so every fake identity earns too little to cover its own bond, while trust-weighted non-kin graders refuse to amplify unvouched newcomers. Faking a thousand agents therefore means posting a thousand separate bonds, and one exposed fake gets slashed into a net loss.
